rows.grounds: compound expressing a total of forty-two parts; dvayādhikya qualifies catvāriṃśat
absolutive indicating prior action of division or measurement
compound of gṛha and unnata denoting the elevation of the structure

items.question: Into how many proportional parts must the total house height be divided?
premises: The house height is the object of proportional division.
The division is specified as forty increased by two parts.
The action of making this division is expressed by an absolutive.
items.inference: The total height of the house must be divided into forty-two proportional parts.
uncertainties: The precise architectural referent of gṛhonnata in this context is inferred from surrounding measurement verses.
items.plain_english: Having divided the total height of the house into forty-two parts.
